title: Exercise 7B · Q6
summary: The horizontal gap and the height difference are the two shorter sides.
alt: Exercise 7B · Q6: Two vertical buildings of heights 30 m and 37 m are 16 m apart. A cable is pulled taut and attached from the top of one building to the top of the other building. Find the length of the cable.

hyp.label: Hypotenuse
hyp.text: The side opposite the right angle. It is always the longest side.

legA.label: Shorter side 1
legA.text: One of the two sides that meet at the right angle.

legB.label: Shorter side 2
legB.text: The other side that meets at the right angle.

steps.title: The question
steps.narration: Two vertical buildings of heights **30 m** and **37 m** are **16 m** apart. A cable **AB** is pulled taut from the top of one building to the top of the other. Taking **C** level with **A**, **∠C = 90°**. Find the length of the cable.

steps.title: Height difference
steps.narration: First find the vertical side **BC** — the difference in the building heights.\[\begin{aligned}\role{legB}{BC} &= 37 - 30 = \role{legB}{7}\ \text{m}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Spot the right angle
steps.narration: In ΔABC, **∠C = 90°**, so the **hypotenuse** is the side opposite it: **the cable AB**. The other two sides meet at the right angle.

steps.title: Pythagoras' theorem
steps.narration: **Pythagoras' theorem**: the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{AB^2} &= \role{legA}{AC^2} + \role{legB}{BC^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Substitute the lengths
steps.narration: Replace each side by its length.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{AB^2} &= \role{legA}{AC^2} + \role{legB}{BC^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{16^2} + \role{legB}{7^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Square and add
steps.narration: Square each number, then add them.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{AB^2} &= \role{legA}{AC^2} + \role{legB}{BC^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{16^2} + \role{legB}{7^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{256} + \role{legB}{49} \\ &= \role{hyp}{305}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Square root
steps.narration: 305 is not a perfect square, so use a calculator and round to 3 significant figures.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{AB^2} &= \role{legA}{AC^2} + \role{legB}{BC^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{16^2} + \role{legB}{7^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{256} + \role{legB}{49} \\ &= \role{hyp}{305} \\ \role{hyp}{AB} &= \sqrt{305} = \role{ans}{17.5\ \text{m}}\end{aligned}\]

formulas.title: Pythagoras' theorem
formulas.text: In a right-angled triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.

formulas.title: Finding the hypotenuse
formulas.text: Add the two squares, then take the square root.

formulas.title: Finding a shorter side
formulas.text: Subtract the known shorter side's square from the hypotenuse's square, then take the square root.

challenges.title: Now you try
challenges.prompt: Two buildings **8 m** apart have heights **9 m** and **15 m**. Find the cable joining their tops.
challenges.hint: Height difference = 15 − 9 = 6 m; horizontal gap = 8 m.
challenges.explain: Height difference = 6 m, horizontal = 8 m, so cable = √(8²+6²) = √100 = 10 m.

takeaways: Find the **right angle** first — the side opposite it is the **hypotenuse**.
To find the hypotenuse: **add** the squares of the two shorter sides, then take the **square root**.
The hypotenuse is always the **longest** side, so check that your answer is bigger than both of the other sides.

notes.title: Exam tip
notes.text: Always begin with a line such as "In ΔABC, ∠C = 90°. Using Pythagoras' Theorem," — it shows which triangle and which right angle you are using.

notes.title: Rounding
notes.text: If the answer is not a whole number, give it to **3 significant figures** unless the question says otherwise.
